claims.text: Sustained loading induces progressively evolving nanoscale elastic-field undulations at FCC/BCC layer interfaces.
Increasing the lattice mismatch between adjacent layers promotes formation of the elastic-field undulations.
Elastic-field undulations eventually evolve into twin boundaries.
The resulting twin boundaries mediate plastic deformation at the multilayer interfaces.
The degree of interlayer lattice mismatch directly governs the threshold stress for onset of the proposed instability.
The mismatch-dependent instability threshold controls the transition from elastic accommodation to progressive plastic flow under creep conditions.
The proposed initial material is a nanoscale coating with alternating FCC and BCC HEA layers and initial interlayer coherency.
High-strain-rate loading can be combined with sustained creep loading to test the proposed mechanism.
Small compositional adjustments can systematically vary interfacial lattice mismatch while retaining the multilayer architecture.
Testing from cryogenic to moderate temperatures will expose different creep regimes.
Severe lattice distortion and interfacial mismatch generate elastic undulations with a characteristic wavelength of approximately 1–2 nm.
As applied stress increases, the undulations localize strain and transform into interfacial twin boundaries.
The emerging nanoscale features distribute dislocation-nucleation sites.
Distributed dislocation nucleation enables progressive plastic flow while maintaining overall strength.
Higher-mismatch samples will have a lower threshold stress for initiation of nanoscale elastic undulations than lower-mismatch samples.
Higher-mismatch samples will form twin boundaries earlier and more broadly than lower-mismatch samples.
Undulation patterns approximately 1–2 nm wide will appear before significant creep deformation.
Low-mismatch, highly coherent multilayers will have a higher undulation threshold and less pronounced twin-boundary evolution.
The mechanism is expected to apply only when nanoscale layer spacing and compositional tuning preserve measurable interfacial mismatch.
The mechanism may cease to dominate at high temperature when thermally activated deformation or recovery dominates, or when multilayer fidelity is poor.
